questions.stem: A tangent and a chord meet at a point on the circumference. The angle between the tangent and the chord is $55°$. What is the angle in the alternate segment?
questions.explanation: By the alternate segment theorem, the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment. Both are $55°$.

questions.stem: Two tangents are drawn from an external point to a circle. The angle between the two tangents is $50°$. What is the angle subtended at the centre by the two radii to the points of tangency?
questions.explanation: The tangent meets the radius at $90°$ at each point of tangency. The four angles in the quadrilateral formed by the two tangents and two radii sum to $360°$. So the centre angle is $360° - 90° - 90° - 50° = 130°$.
